title: Pizza Salame Piccante
subtitle: Spicy salami pizza with chilli oil
excerpt: Pizza salame piccante is a tomato and mozzarella pizza loaded with sliced spicy salami and finished with chilli-infused olive oil. The salami crisps slightly at the edges in a very hot oven, and the chilli oil is added after baking so it does not burn.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dough 24 hours ahead. Make the chilli oil at least 30 minutes before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum setting. Preheat with a heavy tray or pizza stone for at least 45 minutes.

content.text: This pizza is a straightforward combination of tomato sauce, mozzarella, and spicy cured salami, finished with chilli oil after baking. The salami gives you fat and heat from the pork; the chilli oil adds a second layer of spice and gloss. It comes together in under 15 minutes if the dough is already made and the oven is hot.
You need one 210 g ball of 24-hour pizza dough per pizza, rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.

items.prepNote: use spicy salami or nduja-seasoned prosciutto if you can find it; regular prosciutto also works

content.text: Warm the olive oil in a small pan over very low heat. Add the chilli flakes and heat for 1 minute until the oil turns orange. Do not let the chilli blacken. Remove from the heat and leave to cool. The oil keeps in a jar at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
Heat the oven to its maximum setting with a heavy tray or pizza stone on the top shelf. Preheat for at least 45 minutes.
Season the passata with salt. Stretch one dough ball to a rough 30 cm disc.
Spread the passata over the base and scatter the mozzarella. Lay the salami slices over the cheese.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the rim is charred and the salami is beginning to crisp at the edges. Drizzle with chilli oil and eat immediately.

Salame piccante pizza is common across southern and central Italy. The Calabrian version uses the local nduja, a very soft spicy sausage that melts into the mozzarella when it bakes. The home version uses whatever spicy cured pork is available. The chilli oil at the end is the step that ties it together.
